## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Format | Standard (Arena BO1) |
| Colors | Sultai (Blue / Black / Green) |
| Archetype | Graveyard combo-midrange |
| Size | 60 cards (35 spells, 25 lands) |
| Primary win | Unblockable, graveyard-sized Souls of the Lost |
| Secondary win | Season of Loss life-drain and the Atlantis Attacks Leviathan |

## Overview

**Grave Team Six** fuses two mechanics into one engine: **Fathomless descent**
(your graveyard's permanent count X makes creatures huge and spells brutal) and
**Teamwork** (tap creatures with total power N to unlock the second mode of a
spell). The bridge between the two is *Souls of the Lost* — its power literally
equals the number of permanent cards in your graveyard, which makes it the
perfect creature to tap for Teamwork costs, over and over again.

Every fetchland, surveil land, looting artifact, and mill spell in the deck
doubles as fuel: each permanent in the graveyard makes Souls bigger, makes
Terror Tide and Chupacabra Echo wipe harder, lets Squirming Emergence reanimate
bigger things, and turns Matzalantli's back face — the land The Core — into a
mana engine. Teamwork spells then convert that giant board presence into
reanimation, removal, counterspells, and a 6/5 hexproof Leviathan.

## Approach

### Game plan phases

1. **Dig (turns 1-3).** Play fetchlands and crack them, surveil with
   Undercity Sewers / Hedge Maze / Underground Mortuary, cast Cache Grab or
   Song of Stupefaction to mill, and loot with Matzalantli, the Great Door.
   Every permanent that hits the graveyard counts.
2. **Grow (turns 3-5).** Souls of the Lost becomes a 5/6 or 6/7. Tap it (and
   Solemn Simulacrum or Chupacabra Echo) to pay Teamwork costs: Too Evil to
   Stay Dead reanimates anything, Cruel Alliance exiles any creature and gains
   life, We Say Thee Nay! hard-counters, Go Nuts! fights and pumps.
3. **Win (turn 5+).** Reanimate with Squirming Emergence and Earth's Mightiest
   Heroes, clear the board with Terror Tide (Souls survives as X+1 toughness),
   then kill with Rogue's Passage plus a giant Souls, Season of Loss draining
   for your creature count, or the hexproof Leviathan.

### Card roles

| Role | Cards |
|---|---|
| Engine | Souls of the Lost, Matzalantli the Great Door, Squirming Emergence, Too Evil to Stay Dead, Cache Grab, Insidious Roots |
| GY enablers | Evolving Wilds, Terramorphic Expanse, Fabled Passage, surveil lands, Song of Stupefaction, Solemn Simulacrum |
| Payoffs | Terror Tide, Chupacabra Echo, Season of Loss, Atlantis Attacks, Rogue's Passage, Restless Reef |
| Teamwork tappers | Souls of the Lost, Solemn Simulacrum, Chupacabra Echo, Restless Reef, Restless Vinestalk |

### Lands as engines

| Land | Engine role |
|---|---|
| Rogue's Passage | Win con: makes the giant Souls unblockable for lethal |
| Restless Reef | 4/4 deathtouch attacker that mills four on attack (GY fuel) |
| Restless Vinestalk | 5/5 trample attacker; sets another creature to 3/3 on attack |
| Evolving Wilds / Terramorphic Expanse / Fabled Passage | Sacrificed lands are permanents in the graveyard: direct Fathomless fuel |
| Surveil duals (Sewers / Maze / Mortuary) | Surveil 1 puts lands and spells into the graveyard |
| The Core (Matzalantli back face) | Legendary land that taps for X mana of any color |

### Curve and mana

Average CMC is about 3.1. The deck is black-heavy with green support and a
light blue touch, matching the mana base: five UB lands, five UG lands, three
BG surveil lands, seven fetchlands, and five basics. Fetchlands thin the deck
and always count as a permanent in the graveyard after cracking.

## Gameplay strategy

### Early game

Prioritize a fetchland or surveil land on turn one. Turn two, either Souls of
the Lost (discard a redundant land) or Song of Stupefaction / Cache Grab to
start the graveyard. Do not hold back graveyard fuel — X grows fast, and every
point matters for Souls, Terror Tide, and Squirming Emergence.

### Mid game

With four or five permanents in the graveyard, Souls is a real threat and
Teamwork costs are trivial to pay. Reanimate a Solemn Simulacrum to ramp and
draw, or loop Matzalantli for card selection. Use Cruel Alliance and
Chupacabra Echo to keep the opponent's board small while your graveyard grows.

### The combo turn

1. Graveyard has 10+ permanents: Souls of the Lost is an 11/12.
2. Tap Souls plus one other creature to cast Too Evil to Stay Dead with
   Teamwork — return the best creature card in your graveyard (often another
   Souls or Solemn).
3. Cast Squirming Emergence (X = 10+): return Matzalantli or a creature.
4. Attack: activate Rogue's Passage on Souls. 11+ unblockable damage, often
   lethal. If they survive, Terror Tide next turn clears everything while
   Souls survives as X+1 toughness.

### Win condition 2: Season of Loss and the Leviathan

Season of Loss with {P}{P}{P} makes each opponent lose life equal to the number
of creature cards in your graveyard — commonly 8 to 12. The {P} mode forces
sacrifices to clear blockers, and {P}{P} refills your hand if creatures died
this turn. Atlantis Attacks (cast with Teamwork) creates a 6/5 hexproof
Leviathan and bounces two permanents — a resilient finisher that dodges spot
removal. Restless Reef and Restless Vinestalk close out games when the
opponent is low.

### Mulligan guide

Keep: two to three lands, plus any of Souls of the Lost, Cache Grab, Song of
Stupefaction, Matzalantli, or a reanimation spell. A hand with no graveyard
fuel and no two-drop is a mulligan. Ship hands full of six- and seven-mana
spells. Lands that surveil or fetch count as fuel, so land-heavy hands are
better here than in most decks.

### Key interactions and edge cases

- **Souls of the Lost survives your own Terror Tide**: toughness is X+1, so a
  board wipe leaves your biggest creature standing.
- **Matzalantli transforms with four or more permanent types** (artifact,
  creature, enchantment, land, planeswalker, battle) in the graveyard — the
  deck naturally has artifact (Matzalantli, fetchlands), creature, land, and
  enchantment types.
- **Teamwork taps as an additional cost**: tap creatures before the spell
  resolves, so removal in response does not stop the second mode.
- **Cache Grab mills four and returns a permanent card to hand** — instant
  speed, and it is both fuel and recursion in one card.
- **Insidious Roots**: every reanimation makes a Plant, then pumps all Plants;
  Plants also tap for mana, creating a late-game army that pays Teamwork costs.
- **Graveyard hate** (exile effects) is the deck's main weakness: fetchlands
  and mill still work, but keep Cache Grab and draw spells for resilience.

### Matchups

- **Aggro:** Terror Tide, Chupacabra Echo, and Cruel Alliance keep the board
  clear; Souls blocks well. Prioritize graveyard count over speed.
- **Midrange:** win the value war — reanimation loops out-grind most
  midrange decks; Solemn Simulacrum and Squirming Emergence provide card
  advantage.
- **Control:** We Say Thee Nay! protects key spells; Atlantis Attacks and
  recursion from the graveyard are hard for control to answer permanently.
  Rogue's Passage turns any surviving creature into a clock.
